new_findings.summary: Repeated continuation clicks append the same probe page multiple times.
new_findings.failure_scenario: While Show more checks is waiting on a slow response, click it twice. Both calls capture the same moreProbes cursor; each response appends its full page. Attempts then appear twice with duplicate execution_ref React keys and duplicated recovery controls. A late duplicate response can also restore an already-consumed cursor. This is display/navigation noise, not a demonstrated duplicate execution or authority bypass.
new_findings.evidence: CONFIRMED at the handler level: a fresh Node probe evaluated the source loadMoreProbes body (only the TypeScript catch annotation removed), held two continuation responses, then released both; rows became p-1,p-2,p-2. The button has no loading/disabled guard. This was not a live-browser reproduction.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Allow only one continuation request per cursor, disable the control while loading, and/or deduplicate appended attempts by execution_ref. Do not let an obsolete response overwrite a newer cursor.
